title: Accountants and auditors
rationale: Purely knowledge-based office work involving financial analysis, tax preparation, and auditing. No meaningful physical component that robots would automate.

title: Actors
rationale: Performance is fundamentally human—audiences value human emotional expression and physicality. Some CGI/motion-capture technology exists but live performance and on-camera acting remain human domains requiring constant creative improvisation.

title: Actuaries
rationale: Entirely desk-based analytical work using mathematics, statistics, and financial modeling. No physical component to automate.

title: Administrative services and facilities managers
rationale: Primarily office-based management and coordination work. Some facility oversight involves physical inspection, but the role is fundamentally about planning, directing, and supervising rather than physical labor.

title: Adult basic and secondary education and ESL teachers
rationale: Teaching adults in classroom settings is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical tasks amenable to robotic automation.

title: Advertising sales agents
rationale: Sales work involving client meetings, presentations, and relationship building. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical labor component.

title: Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers
rationale: Strategic planning, creative direction, and team management. Purely knowledge work with no physical automation potential.

title: Aerospace engineering and operations technologists and technicians
rationale: Involves hands-on installation, calibration, and testing of aerospace equipment in controlled but variable environments. Some routine testing and calibration tasks are increasingly automated, but the variety of systems and precision requirements still need human technicians for many tasks.

title: Aerospace engineers
rationale: Design, analysis, and testing oversight work that is primarily computational and knowledge-based. Physical prototyping and testing is done by technicians.

title: Agricultural and food science technicians
rationale: Laboratory and field work involving sample collection, testing, and equipment operation. Routine lab analysis is increasingly automated, but fieldwork and novel experimental setups still require human adaptability.

title: Agricultural and food scientists
rationale: Primarily research, analysis, and oversight work. Some fieldwork but the role is fundamentally about scientific inquiry and knowledge application rather than physical labor.

title: Agricultural engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based. May visit farms and facilities but the role centers on designing systems rather than physical labor.

title: Agricultural workers
rationale: By 2031, robotic harvesting covers an expanded range of crops on large-scale operations, and automated planting/spraying is widespread. However, many crops still require human dexterity for harvest, and small/medium farms with variable terrain need human workers for exceptions and diverse tasks.

title: Air traffic controllers
rationale: Highly cognitive work involving real-time decision-making in safety-critical environments. While the work environment is physical (control towers), the actual task is purely mental coordination and communication. Automation assists but human judgment remains essential.

title: Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians
rationale: Skilled hands-on work in variable configurations—each aircraft has unique wear patterns and issues. Diagnostics increasingly automated, but physical repair work in tight spaces with diverse components requires human dexterity and judgment. Safety-critical nature slows automation adoption.

title: Airline and commercial pilots
rationale: Autopilot handles much of routine flight, but pilots remain essential for safety oversight, emergency response, and complex operations. Regulatory and public trust barriers remain high. Autonomous cargo flights may begin but passenger flights still require human pilots.

title: Animal care and service workers
rationale: Working with live animals requires constant adaptation to unpredictable behavior. Animals need trust-based relationships with handlers. Environments vary widely from kennels to veterinary offices to outdoor settings. Robots cannot yet manage the variability and emotional sensitivity required.

title: Announcers and DJs
rationale: On-air broadcasting is primarily verbal and creative. While AI-generated voices exist, live announcing requires real-time improvisation and human personality. The physical component (sitting at a microphone) is minimal.

title: Anthropologists and archeologists
rationale: Primarily research and analysis work. Archaeological fieldwork involves physical digging but in highly variable, novel environments where each site is unique. The intellectual interpretation is the core of the work.

title: Arbitrators, mediators, and conciliators
rationale: Entirely interpersonal and cognitive work involving dispute resolution, negotiation, and legal reasoning. No physical component.

title: Architects
rationale: Design work that is primarily computational and creative. Site visits occur but the role is fundamentally about design, planning, and client communication.

title: Architectural and engineering managers
rationale: Management and oversight role that is entirely knowledge-based. Involves planning, coordinating, and directing technical projects.

title: Archivists, curators, and museum workers
rationale: Conservators perform delicate physical work on unique, irreplaceable artifacts requiring extreme care and judgment. Museum technicians handle installation in variable spaces. The uniqueness of each object and environment limits automation potential significantly.

title: Art directors
rationale: Creative management and visual direction work. Entirely knowledge and aesthetic judgment based with no physical automation potential.

title: Assemblers and fabricators
rationale: By 2031, robotic assembly systems handle the large majority of repetitive assembly tasks across manufacturing. Human workers focus on complex assemblies, quality exceptions, and tasks requiring unusual dexterity. Standardized assembly lines are heavily automated.

title: Athletes and sports competitors
rationale: Athletic performance is inherently human—audiences value human competition. While training technology advances, the actual performance is entirely about human physical capability and cannot be replaced by robots.

title: Athletic trainers
rationale: Hands-on physical assessment and treatment of athletes in highly variable situations. Each injury and athlete is different, requiring skilled touch, trust, and real-time judgment. The interpersonal and diagnostic aspects resist automation.

title: Atmospheric scientists, including meteorologists
rationale: Purely analytical and computational work involving weather modeling and forecasting. No physical labor component.

title: Audiologists
rationale: Clinical work requiring patient interaction, physical examination of ears, and fitting of hearing devices. Each patient presents unique anatomy and needs. Trust and communication are essential components.

title: Automotive body and glass repairers
rationale: Each vehicle presents unique damage patterns requiring assessment and custom repair approaches. Some standardized repairs (windshield replacement) are becoming more automated, but body work requires significant human judgment and dexterity for variable damage.

title: Automotive service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Diagnostics increasingly automated, but physical repair work varies enormously by vehicle, problem, and environment. Working in tight engine compartments with diverse fasteners and components requires human dexterity. Shops vary widely in layout and equipment.

title: Bakers
rationale: Commercial/industrial baking is increasingly automated with robotic mixing, shaping, and packaging. Large bakeries and chain operations use extensive automation. Artisanal and custom baking still requires human skill, but the majority of volume production is automatable by 2031.

title: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists
rationale: Highly personal service requiring trust, communication, creative judgment, and skilled dexterity on unique human heads. Each client's hair, preferences, and head shape differ. The social and aesthetic aspects are core to the service. Very resistant to robotic automation.

title: Bartenders
rationale: Robotic bartending systems exist for standardized drinks in high-volume venues. However, craft cocktail preparation, customer interaction, and the social nature of bartending in most establishments still require humans. The hospitality and improvisation aspects resist full automation.

title: Bill and account collectors
rationale: Office-based work involving phone calls, correspondence, and negotiation. Entirely knowledge and communication work with no physical component.

title: Biochemists and biophysicists
rationale: Lab work involves some physical manipulation of equipment and samples, with automated lab systems handling routine procedures. However, novel experimental design and non-standard protocols still require human researchers. The core intellectual work is not physical.

title: Bioengineers and biomedical engineers
rationale: Primarily design and engineering work that is knowledge-based. Some prototype testing involves physical work, but the role centers on design, analysis, and problem-solving.

title: Biological technicians
rationale: Laboratory work with increasing automation of routine procedures like sample preparation, testing, and data collection. However, novel experimental setups and troubleshooting still require human technicians. Automated lab systems handle much of the standardized work.

title: Boilermakers
rationale: Heavy industrial work in variable environments—power plants, refineries, ships. Each installation is different, requiring skilled welding and metalwork in confined spaces. The variability of work sites and need for skilled judgment limits automation, though some routine welding tasks are automated.

title: Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks
rationale: Entirely desk-based data entry and record-keeping work. No physical component. Already heavily digitized.

title: Broadcast, sound, and video technicians
rationale: Technical work setting up and operating audio/video equipment in variable venues and studios. Each setup is different, requiring troubleshooting and adaptation. Some studio operations are increasingly automated, but live event work requires human adaptability.

title: Budget analysts
rationale: Purely analytical office work involving financial planning and budget review. No physical component.

title: Bus drivers
rationale: Autonomous vehicle technology covers many fixed routes by 2031, especially dedicated bus lanes and highway segments. However, complex urban environments, passenger assistance, and safety oversight still require human drivers for many routes. School bus drivers face additional trust and regulatory barriers.

title: Butchers
rationale: Industrial meat processing is heavily automated with robotic cutting, deboning, and packaging systems. Custom retail butchering still requires human skill for variable cuts and customer interaction, but the majority of meat processing volume is increasingly automated.

title: Calibration technologists and technicians
rationale: Routine calibration of standardized equipment is increasingly automated, but technicians still needed for diverse equipment types, field calibration, and troubleshooting. The variety of instruments and environments provides some protection from full automation.

title: Cardiovascular technologists and technicians
rationale: Patient-facing medical work requiring trust and physical positioning of patients and equipment. Each patient's anatomy varies. Imaging automation assists but human operators needed for patient interaction, positioning, and clinical judgment.

title: Career and technical education teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal work. While some shop/lab teaching involves physical demonstration, the core is human instruction and mentorship. No significant physical automation potential.

title: Carpenters
rationale: Residential and custom carpentry involves highly variable environments—each building, renovation, and design is different. While some prefabrication and CNC work is automated, on-site carpentry requires constant adaptation to existing structures and conditions. Commercial construction has more standardized tasks.

title: Cartographers and photogrammetrists
rationale: Primarily digital/computational work using GIS software and satellite imagery. Some fieldwork for ground-truthing but the role is fundamentally desk-based analysis and map creation.

title: Cashiers
rationale: Self-checkout and automated payment systems are widespread by 2031. Many retail and fast-food locations operate with minimal cashier staff. However, some customer-facing roles remain for complex transactions, customer assistance, and stores where human interaction is valued.

title: Chefs and head cooks
rationale: Executive chefs focus on menu creation, kitchen management, and quality control—largely creative and managerial. While robotic kitchen systems handle some routine cooking in chains, head chefs in restaurants provide creative direction and handle complex preparations that require taste, judgment, and improvisation.

title: Chemical engineers
rationale: Design and process engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational. Plant visits occur but the role is about design and optimization, not physical labor.

title: Chemical technicians
rationale: Laboratory work with increasing automation of routine testing and analysis. Automated systems handle standardized procedures, but technicians still needed for sample preparation, equipment maintenance, and non-routine testing.

title: Chemists and materials scientists
rationale: Research work with some physical lab components. Automated lab systems handle routine synthesis and testing, but novel research requires human creativity and adaptation. The core work is intellectual.

title: Childcare workers
rationale: Caring for young children requires constant human attention, emotional sensitivity, and improvisation. Each child's needs differ moment to moment. Parents require deep trust in caregivers. Among the most resistant occupations to physical automation.

title: Chiropractors
rationale: Hands-on therapeutic work requiring skilled touch, patient communication, and real-time judgment based on each patient's unique physiology. Trust between practitioner and patient is essential. Very resistant to robotic automation.

title: Civil engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Mix of office-based design work and field testing/inspection. Field work involves variable sites and conditions. Some testing is automated but site inspection and field measurement in diverse environments requires human adaptability.

title: Civil engineers
rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and project management work. Site visits occur but the role is fundamentally about engineering design and oversight.

title: Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators
rationale: Mostly office-based analytical work. Some field inspection of damage sites, but the core work is reviewing claims and making determinations. Physical inspection increasingly supplemented by drones and photographic evidence.

title: Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians
rationale: Clinical lab work is increasingly automated with robotic sample handling, automated analyzers, and AI-assisted diagnostics. High-volume standardized tests are largely automated. Technologists focus on complex tests, quality control, and troubleshooting automated systems.

title: Coaches and scouts
rationale: Coaching involves interpersonal leadership, motivation, strategy, and real-time decision-making during competitions. While analytics and video technology assist, the human connection and leadership aspects are core. Minimal physical automation potential.

title: Community health workers
rationale: Interpersonal outreach and health education work in community settings. Entirely about human connection, trust-building, and communication. No physical automation potential.

title: Compensation and benefits managers
rationale: Office-based management work involving policy development and administration. Purely knowledge work.

title: Compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialists
rationale: Analytical office work involving job analysis and compensation planning. No physical component.

title: Compliance officers
rationale: Regulatory review and oversight work that is entirely knowledge-based. Some facility inspections but the core is analytical.

title: Computer and information research scientists
rationale: Purely knowledge work involving research, algorithm development, and computational analysis. No physical component.

title: Computer and information systems managers
rationale: IT management and strategic planning. Purely knowledge and management work.

title: Computer hardware engineers
rationale: Design work that is primarily knowledge-based. Some prototype testing and lab work, but the core role is design and analysis.

title: Computer network architects
rationale: Network design and planning work that is entirely knowledge-based and digital.

title: Computer programmers
rationale: Entirely digital work involving writing and testing code. No physical component.

title: Computer support specialists
rationale: Mostly remote/desk-based troubleshooting. Some physical hardware setup and repair, but increasingly handled remotely. The physical component is minor.

title: Computer systems analysts
rationale: Analytical work designing and improving IT systems. Purely knowledge work.

title: Concierges
rationale: Customer-facing service role requiring interpersonal skills, local knowledge, and problem-solving. Some tasks (information lookup, reservations) are digitized, but the personal service and human interaction aspects are central. Minimal physical labor.

title: Conservation scientists and foresters
rationale: Research and management work primarily involving analysis and planning. Some fieldwork in natural environments, but the role is about scientific assessment and policy rather than physical labor.

title: Construction and building inspectors
rationale: Field inspection work in variable construction environments. Each site and building is unique. While drones and sensors assist, physical access to inspect structural elements, electrical systems, and plumbing in diverse configurations still requires human presence and judgment.

title: Construction equipment operators
rationale: Large-scale earthmoving and grading increasingly automated with GPS-guided autonomous equipment on structured sites. Excavation and routine operations on large commercial projects use autonomous or semi-autonomous machines. Complex operations in tight spaces or variable terrain still need human operators.

title: Construction laborers and helpers
rationale: Repetitive tasks on structured construction sites (material handling, site cleanup, concrete work) increasingly automated. However, the variety of tasks, changing environments, and need to work alongside human tradespeople in variable conditions means humans still needed for many tasks.

title: Construction managers
rationale: Management and coordination role. While overseeing increasingly automated job sites, the role itself is about planning, scheduling, problem-solving, and human coordination. Minimal physical labor.

title: Cooks
rationale: Chain restaurant and institutional cooking increasingly automated with robotic kitchen systems handling standardized recipes. Fast-food preparation is highly automatable. However, varied menu items, special orders, and non-chain restaurants still require human cooks for adaptation and quality.

title: Correctional officers and bailiffs
rationale: Security and supervision of inmates requires constant human judgment, de-escalation skills, and physical presence in unpredictable environments. Surveillance technology assists but the interpersonal and safety aspects require human officers. Trust and authority dynamics are inherently human.

title: Cost estimators
rationale: Analytical work involving project cost analysis and estimation. Primarily desk-based knowledge work. Some site visits but the core work is analytical.

title: Court reporters and simultaneous captioners
rationale: Transcription work that is increasingly digital. While physically present in courtrooms, the work is capturing spoken words, not physical labor.

title: Craft and fine artists
rationale: Artisanal creation involving unique creative vision and skilled handwork with novel materials and techniques. Each piece is unique. The creative and improvisational aspects are core. Audiences value human-made art. Very resistant to physical automation.

title: Credit counselors
rationale: Advisory and counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Customer service representatives
rationale: Office/call-center work involving communication and problem-solving. While increasingly handled by AI chatbots, the remaining human roles are entirely interpersonal, not physical.

title: Dancers and choreographers
rationale: Performance art that is fundamentally about human physical expression and creativity. Audiences value human performers. While motion-capture exists, live dance is inherently human.

title: Data scientists
rationale: Purely digital analytical work involving data analysis, modeling, and programming. No physical component.

title: Database administrators and architects
rationale: Digital work managing and maintaining database systems. No physical component beyond occasional hardware interaction.

title: Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers
rationale: Autonomous delivery vehicles operational on many urban and highway routes by 2031. Last-mile delivery robots handling some residential deliveries. However, complex delivery scenarios (inside buildings, rural areas, customer interaction) still require human drivers. Driver-sales roles have an interpersonal component that resists automation.

title: Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians
rationale: Dental and ophthalmic lab work increasingly automated with CAD/CAM systems, 3D printing, and robotic milling for standardized prosthetics and lenses. Custom and complex cases still need human technicians, but the majority of standard production is highly automated.

title: Dental assistants
rationale: Patient-facing work requiring trust, communication, and assisting dentists in variable clinical situations. Each patient's mouth is different. Chairside assistance requires real-time adaptation. Some sterilization and prep tasks automatable but direct patient care resists automation.

title: Dental hygienists
rationale: Hands-on clinical work in patients' mouths requiring skilled dexterity, patient communication, and real-time adaptation. Each patient's oral anatomy differs. Trust and comfort are essential. While some cleaning tools become more automated, the core work requires human touch and judgment.

title: Dentists
rationale: Complex clinical procedures in highly variable oral environments. Each patient presents unique anatomy and pathology. Robotic dental systems emerging for some standardized procedures, but the diagnostic judgment, patient communication, and procedural adaptation still require human dentists.

title: Desktop publishers
rationale: Entirely digital design and layout work. No physical component.

title: Diagnostic medical sonographers
rationale: Patient-facing imaging work requiring physical manipulation of transducers on patients. Each scan requires real-time adaptation to patient anatomy and pathology. AI assists interpretation but the physical scanning and patient positioning still need human operators who can communicate with patients.

title: Diesel service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Heavy equipment and truck repair in variable conditions. Each vehicle and problem is different. Working on large diesel engines requires significant physical effort and skilled diagnosis. While some diagnostic tools are automated, the physical repair work in diverse configurations resists automation.

title: Dietitians and nutritionists
rationale: Advisory and counseling work about nutrition and diet. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical component.

title: Drafters
rationale: Entirely digital design work using CAD software. No physical component.

title: Drywall installers, ceiling tile installers, and tapers
rationale: Some large commercial drywall installation is becoming automated for uniform walls and ceilings. However, residential work, custom installations, corners, and finishing/taping require human skill and adaptation to each building's unique characteristics.

title: Economists
rationale: Purely analytical and research work. No physical component.

title: Editors
rationale: Knowledge work involving reviewing and improving written content. Entirely digital/desk-based.

title: Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Hands-on testing and repair of electrical/electronic systems in variable configurations. Each system and problem differs. While automated testing equipment handles routine checks, troubleshooting and repair in diverse environments requires human technicians.

title: Electrical and electronics engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.

title: Electrical and electronics installers and repairers
rationale: Installation and repair of electrical equipment in commercial/industrial settings. Some standardized installations are becoming more automated, but the variety of equipment, settings, and fault conditions requires human adaptability. More structured than residential work.

title: Electrical power-line installers and repairers
rationale: Outdoor work on utility lines in highly variable environments—poles, trenches, weather conditions. Each installation and repair scenario is different. Working at heights and in adverse conditions requires human judgment and dexterity. Drones assist inspection but physical line work remains human.

title: Electricians
rationale: Residential and commercial electrical work in highly variable environments. Each building has unique wiring configurations and challenges. Troubleshooting requires creative problem-solving. While some standardized commercial installations see automation, the variety of work resists full automation.

title: Electro-mechanical and mechatronics technologists and technicians
rationale: Testing and maintenance of electromechanical equipment. Routine testing and calibration increasingly automated. However, troubleshooting and repair of diverse systems in various settings still requires human technicians. A mix of automated and human work.

title: Elementary, middle, and high school principals
rationale: School leadership and management work that is entirely administrative, interpersonal, and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Elevator and escalator installers and repairers
rationale: Specialized installation and repair in confined, variable environments. Each building and elevator system presents unique challenges. Safety-critical work requiring skilled mechanical and electrical expertise. The variability of installations and safety requirements limit automation.

title: Emergency management directors
rationale: Planning, coordination, and leadership during emergencies. Entirely managerial and knowledge-based work.

title: EMTs and paramedics
rationale: Emergency medical response in highly unpredictable, novel environments. Each emergency is unique—accident scenes, homes, public spaces. Requires rapid human judgment, physical improvisation, and patient trust. Among the most resistant occupations to physical automation.

title: Entertainment and recreation managers
rationale: Management and business oversight work. Purely administrative and interpersonal.

title: Environmental engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Field testing and monitoring work in variable environments. Each site has unique conditions. While automated monitoring equipment handles routine data collection, field sampling and site assessment in diverse environments requires human adaptability.

title: Environmental engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based. Some field visits but the role centers on analysis and design.

title: Environmental science and protection technicians
rationale: Field sampling and monitoring in variable natural environments. Each site is unique. Automated sensors handle routine monitoring, but field collection, site assessment, and equipment deployment in diverse conditions requires human adaptability.

title: Environmental scientists and specialists
rationale: Research and analysis work with some fieldwork. The role is primarily about scientific assessment and policy recommendation rather than physical labor.

title: Epidemiologists
rationale: Purely analytical research work involving disease pattern analysis. No physical component.

title: Exercise physiologists
rationale: Hands-on patient assessment and exercise program supervision. Each patient has unique physical conditions and needs. Requires trust, communication, and real-time adaptation to patient responses. The interpersonal and clinical judgment aspects resist automation.

title: Farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural managers
rationale: Management role overseeing increasingly automated farm operations. While farm equipment is increasingly autonomous, farmers still make critical decisions about planting, livestock management, and operations in variable conditions. The management and judgment aspects are more important than physical labor.

title: Fashion designers
rationale: Creative design work that is primarily conceptual and digital. While garment production is physical, design itself is knowledge and creativity based.

title: Film and video editors and camera operators
rationale: Camera operation involves physical equipment handling in variable environments, but editing is entirely digital. Automated cameras handle some standardized shots, but creative cinematography requires human artistic vision. Editing is purely digital knowledge work.

title: Financial analysts
rationale: Purely analytical desk-based work involving financial modeling and analysis. No physical component.

title: Financial clerks
rationale: Office-based clerical work involving financial record processing. No physical component.

title: Financial examiners
rationale: Regulatory review and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based with occasional site visits.

title: Financial managers
rationale: Management of financial operations. Purely knowledge and leadership work.

title: Fire inspectors
rationale: Field inspection and investigation in variable buildings and fire scenes. Each scene is unique. While some monitoring technology assists, physical inspection of diverse structures and investigation of fire causes requires human judgment and adaptability.

title: Firefighters
rationale: Emergency response in highly unpredictable, dangerous, novel environments. Each fire and rescue scenario is unique. Requires constant physical improvisation, teamwork, and split-second human judgment. Robotic assistance for specific tasks (hazmat, reconnaissance drones) but human firefighters essential.

title: Fishing and hunting workers
rationale: Work on water in highly variable natural conditions. Each fishing trip involves different weather, seas, and catch conditions. Commercial fishing operations see some automation of processing, but actual fishing in open water with variable conditions requires human judgment and physical adaptability.

title: Fitness trainers and instructors
rationale: Interpersonal work motivating and guiding exercise. Requires personal connection, real-time form assessment, and adaptation to individual clients. While fitness apps and AI coaching exist, in-person training is about human motivation and physical guidance.

title: Flight attendants
rationale: Safety-critical role requiring passenger interaction, emergency response, and service in the confined, variable environment of aircraft cabins. Trust and human presence are essential for passenger safety and comfort. Regulatory requirements mandate human crew.

title: Flooring installers and tile and stone setters
rationale: Skilled installation work in variable residential and commercial spaces. Each floor, wall, and layout is different. Requires precise dexterity and adaptation to existing structures. Some large commercial flooring projects see limited automation, but custom tile work remains human.

title: Floral designers
rationale: Creative arrangement of natural materials that vary in shape, size, and condition. Each arrangement is custom. While simple bouquet assembly could be partially automated, creative floral design requires artistic judgment and handling of fragile, variable natural materials.

title: Food and beverage serving and related workers
rationale: Robotic serving systems operational in some chain restaurants and high-volume venues. Automated drink dispensing and food runners in standardized environments. However, full-service restaurant work requiring customer interaction, carrying multiple plates through crowded spaces, and personalized service still needs humans.

title: Food preparation workers
rationale: Routine food prep tasks (chopping, mixing, portioning) increasingly automated in chain restaurants and institutional kitchens. Robotic prep systems handle standardized ingredients. Human workers focus on quality control and non-standard preparations. High-volume operations are substantially automated.

title: Food processing equipment workers
rationale: Factory-based food processing is highly automated with robotic systems handling sorting, cutting, packaging, and quality inspection. Standardized processing lines operate with minimal human intervention. Humans supervise and handle exceptions. Tobacco processing similarly automated.

title: Food service managers
rationale: Management role overseeing increasingly automated kitchen and service operations. The role itself is about planning, staffing, quality control, and customer relations rather than physical labor.

title: Forensic science technicians
rationale: Crime scene work in highly variable environments—each scene is unique. Lab analysis is increasingly automated, but scene investigation, evidence collection, and documentation in diverse locations requires human judgment and careful physical work.

title: Forest and conservation workers
rationale: Outdoor work in highly variable natural environments. Tasks include planting, trail maintenance, and fire management in forests with diverse terrain. Some planting operations automated on cleared land, but most forest work requires human adaptability to unpredictable natural conditions.

title: Fundraisers
rationale: Interpersonal and strategic work involving donor relations and campaign planning. Entirely knowledge and relationship based.

title: Funeral service workers
rationale: Sensitive service work requiring extreme interpersonal care and trust. Physical tasks include preparation and ceremony management, but the human sensitivity and trust required makes this highly resistant to automation. Each service is unique and emotionally charged.

title: Gambling services workers
rationale: Casino floor work involving equipment operation and customer interaction. Some gaming operations (slot machine monitoring) increasingly automated. Table game dealers require dexterity and customer engagement. The entertainment and hospitality aspects resist full automation.

title: General maintenance and repair workers
rationale: Variable work across many building systems—plumbing, electrical, HVAC, painting. Each repair is different. Some routine maintenance tasks (cleaning, basic checks) automated, but the variety of problems and environments encountered by general maintenance workers requires human adaptability.

title: General office clerks
rationale: Office-based administrative work that is entirely knowledge-based. Filing, data entry, and correspondence. No physical component beyond basic office activities.

title: Genetic counselors
rationale: Patient-facing counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Geographers
rationale: Research and analysis work. Primarily desk-based knowledge work using GIS and data analysis.

title: Geological and hydrologic technicians
rationale: Field work collecting samples and operating equipment in variable geological environments. Each site has unique conditions. While automated sensors and drilling equipment handle some routine operations, field work in diverse terrain requires human adaptability.

title: Geoscientists
rationale: Research work with some fieldwork. The role is primarily about scientific analysis and interpretation rather than physical labor.

title: Glaziers
rationale: Installation of glass in variable buildings and structures. Each installation is different. Working with fragile materials at heights and in diverse configurations requires human dexterity and judgment. Some large commercial installations see limited automation for standard windows.

title: Graphic designers
rationale: Entirely digital creative work. No physical component.

title: Grounds maintenance workers
rationale: Commercial lawn mowing and landscape maintenance increasingly automated with robotic mowers and autonomous equipment for large, uniform areas. However, complex landscaping, garden maintenance, and work on varied residential properties still requires human workers. Large commercial grounds substantially automated.

title: Hand laborers and material movers
rationale: Warehouse and logistics material handling heavily automated with robotic systems. Palletizing, sorting, and transport within facilities largely robotic. Human workers handle exceptions, irregularly shaped items, and tasks in non-standardized environments. High-volume facilities operate with minimal human labor.

title: Hazardous materials removal workers
rationale: Removal work in variable and dangerous environments. Each hazmat site is unique. Robotic systems handle some hazmat cleanup (especially radiation), but many situations require human judgment and dexterity in complex, confined spaces. Safety regulations evolving to allow more robotic intervention.

title: Health and safety engineers
rationale: Engineering design and analysis work focused on workplace safety. Primarily knowledge-based with some facility inspections.

title: Health education specialists
rationale: Educational and outreach work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Health information technologists and medical registrars
rationale: Office-based health data management work. Entirely digital and knowledge-based.

title: Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers
rationale: Installation and repair in variable buildings and environments. Each system and building presents unique challenges. Working in tight spaces (attics, crawlspaces) with diverse equipment configurations requires human dexterity and problem-solving. Some standardized commercial installations see limited automation.

title: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers
rationale: Autonomous trucks operational on most interstate routes by 2031. Highway driving largely automated. However, complex urban delivery, loading/unloading, and last-mile navigation still require human drivers for many scenarios. Human role shifting toward complex route segments and customer interaction.

title: Heavy vehicle and mobile equipment service technicians
rationale: Repair and maintenance of large, diverse equipment in variable settings—construction sites, mines, farms. Each machine and problem is different. Working on heavy equipment requires significant physical effort and skilled diagnosis in variable environments.

title: High school teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal work. Classroom instruction, mentoring, and student engagement require human presence and judgment. No significant physical automation potential.

title: Historians
rationale: Research and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Home health and personal care aides
rationale: Routine physical support tasks (lifting, transfers, mobility assistance) see some robotic assistance. However, working in diverse home environments with unique patient needs and the trust required for intimate personal care limits automation. Robotic assistive devices supplement but don't replace human aides.

title: Human resources managers
rationale: Management and strategic planning work that is entirely knowledge and interpersonal based. No physical component.

title: Human resources specialists
rationale: Administrative and interpersonal work involving recruitment, employee relations, and compliance. No physical component.

title: Hydrologists
rationale: Scientific research and analysis work. Primarily desk-based with some fieldwork, but the role centers on data analysis and modeling.

title: Industrial designers
rationale: Creative design work with some physical prototyping. The core work is conceptual design using digital tools. 3D printing and automated prototyping reduce physical work, but design ideation remains human.

title: Industrial engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Technical work in manufacturing environments involving process testing and optimization. Some routine testing automated, but troubleshooting and process improvement in diverse industrial settings requires human analysis and physical presence.

title: Industrial engineers
rationale: Design and optimization of industrial processes. Primarily analytical work with some facility observation. The role is about system design rather than physical labor.

title: Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights
rationale: Maintenance and repair of industrial machinery in factory settings. Some predictive maintenance and routine servicing automated, but troubleshooting breakdowns of diverse equipment requires human skill and judgment. Each machine and failure mode is different.

title: Industrial production managers
rationale: Management of manufacturing operations. Overseeing increasingly automated production, but the role is about planning, coordination, and decision-making rather than physical work.

title: Information clerks
rationale: Customer-facing information roles (reception, hotel front desk). Kiosks and digital interfaces handle many routine information requests. Remaining human roles focus on complex queries and hospitality. Minimal physical labor.

title: Information security analysts
rationale: Entirely digital work involving cybersecurity analysis and protection. No physical component.

title: Instructional coordinators
rationale: Educational planning and curriculum development work. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Insulation workers
rationale: Installation of insulation in buildings. Some large commercial projects with uniform spaces see automated insulation installation. However, residential and variable commercial work in tight spaces (attics, walls, pipes) requires human dexterity and adaptation. Each installation site is different.

title: Insurance sales agents
rationale: Sales and advisory work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Insurance underwriters
rationale: Risk assessment and policy pricing work. Entirely analytical and knowledge-based.

title: Interior designers
rationale: Creative design work that is primarily conceptual and uses digital tools. Site visits occur but the role is about aesthetic design and client communication.

title: Interpreters and translators
rationale: Language work that is entirely cognitive. While AI translation improves, the remaining human roles focus on nuance and cultural context. No physical component.

title: Ironworkers
rationale: Assembly and installation of structural steel in construction. Some standardized steel erection tasks on large commercial projects becoming more automated with robotic welding and placement. However, working at heights in variable configurations requires human judgment and coordination. Each structure is unique.

title: Janitors and building cleaners
rationale: Commercial cleaning of standardized spaces (offices, malls, airports) heavily automated with robotic floor cleaners and automated systems. However, detailed cleaning, restroom maintenance, and work in variable spaces still requires human workers. Large commercial facilities substantially automated.

title: Jewelers and precious stone and metal workers
rationale: Highly skilled artisanal work with precious materials. Each piece requires unique design and precision handwork. Custom jewelry creation and repair involves creative dexterity with variable materials. While some mass production uses automation, craft jewelry work resists automation.

title: Judges and hearing officers
rationale: Legal decision-making work that is entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical component.

title: Kindergarten and elementary school teachers
rationale: Teaching young children requires human presence, emotional sensitivity, and constant improvisation. Each child needs individual attention and care. Among the most interpersonal occupations. No physical automation potential.

title: Labor relations specialists
rationale: Negotiation and mediation work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.

title: Landscape architects
rationale: Design work primarily using digital tools and creative vision. Site visits occur but the role is about design and planning.

title: Lawyers
rationale: Legal analysis, argumentation, and client representation. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.

title: Librarians and library media specialists
rationale: Information management and community service work. While automated book handling systems exist, the role is primarily about knowledge curation, community programs, and patron assistance. Minimal physical component.

title: Library technicians and assistants
rationale: Book handling, shelving, and circulation management. Automated shelving and retrieval systems operational in some large libraries. Self-checkout widespread. However, many libraries still require human staff for physical collection management, especially in older facilities.

title: Licensed practical and licensed vocational nurses
rationale: Patient care requiring trust, communication, and physical assistance in variable clinical settings. Each patient has unique needs. Bedside care, medication administration, and wound care require human judgment and dexterity. Robotic assistance supplements but doesn't replace LPNs.

title: Loan officers
rationale: Financial analysis and client advisory work. Entirely knowledge-based with some client interaction.

title: Lodging managers
rationale: Hotel management involving coordination and customer service. While hotel operations increasingly automated (check-in kiosks, robotic room service), the management role focuses on staff supervision, guest relations, and operational decisions.

title: Logging workers
rationale: Mechanized logging uses increasingly automated equipment. Some harvesting operations use autonomous or semi-autonomous machines on managed timber lands. However, variable terrain, diverse tree species, and environmental conditions require human operators for many situations.

title: Logisticians
rationale: Supply chain planning and optimization work. Primarily analytical and knowledge-based. While overseeing automated logistics systems, the role is about planning and coordination.

title: Machinists and tool and die makers
rationale: CNC machines handle most routine machining with high precision. Automated tool changers and robotic loading widespread. Human machinists focus on complex setups, custom work, and quality control. Tool and die making for unique molds requires more human skill, but standard machining is heavily automated.

title: Management analysts
rationale: Consulting and advisory work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Manicurists and pedicurists
rationale: Intimate personal service requiring dexterity, customer interaction, and trust. Each client's nails and preferences differ. The social and personal nature of the service, combined with detailed work on human hands and feet, strongly resists automation.

title: Marine engineers and naval architects
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.

title: Market research analysts
rationale: Analytical work involving data collection and analysis. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Marriage and family therapists
rationale: Therapeutic counseling work that is entirely interpersonal. No physical component.

title: Masonry workers
rationale: Some large commercial bricklaying projects use robotic bricklaying systems for uniform walls. However, residential work, custom patterns, stone masonry, and repair/restoration require human skill and adaptation. The variety of materials and configurations limits full automation.

title: Massage therapists
rationale: Highly personal hands-on therapy requiring skilled touch, real-time assessment of muscle tension and patient response, and trust. Each client's body is different. The therapeutic relationship and tactile sensitivity are core. Very resistant to robotic automation.

title: Material moving machine operators
rationale: Warehouse and facility material moving heavily automated with autonomous forklifts, AGVs, and robotic palletizers. Large distribution centers and factories use automated material handling systems extensively. Human operators focus on non-standard loads and complex environments.

title: Material recording clerks
rationale: Inventory tracking and warehouse administration increasingly automated with RFID, automated scanning, and warehouse management systems. Physical inventory counts supplemented by drones and automated systems. However, receiving, inspecting, and handling exceptions still requires human workers.

title: Materials engineers
rationale: Research and design work that is primarily knowledge-based. Lab work is secondary to analysis and design.

title: Mathematicians and statisticians
rationale: Purely analytical work involving mathematical modeling and statistical analysis. No physical component.

title: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Hands-on testing and fabrication of mechanical systems. Some routine testing automated, but prototyping, troubleshooting, and testing in variable configurations requires human technicians.

title: Mechanical engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.

title: Medical and health services managers
rationale: Healthcare management and administration. Entirely knowledge and leadership work.

title: Medical assistants
rationale: Patient-facing clinical and administrative work. Each patient interaction differs. Taking vitals, assisting with examinations, and patient communication require human presence and trust. Some routine tasks automated but direct patient care resists automation.

title: Medical dosimetrists
rationale: Highly specialized calculation and planning work for radiation therapy. Primarily computational with some physical treatment planning setup. The core work is analytical.

title: Medical equipment repairers
rationale: Repair and maintenance of diverse medical equipment in hospital settings. Each device and problem is different. Diagnostic tools improving, but physical repair of complex medical devices in clinical environments requires human skill and judgment.

title: Medical records specialists
rationale: Data management work that is entirely digital. No physical component.

title: Medical scientists
rationale: Research work with significant lab components. Automated lab systems handle routine procedures, but novel research design and experimental work requires human creativity. The core work is intellectual inquiry.

title: Medical transcriptionists
rationale: Audio-to-text work that is entirely digital. No physical component. Largely automated by speech recognition.

title: Meeting, convention, and event planners
rationale: Planning and coordination work with some physical setup oversight. The role is primarily about planning, vendor management, and logistics rather than physical labor.

title: Metal and plastic machine workers
rationale: CNC machines and robotic systems handle most routine metal and plastic machining, stamping, and molding. Automated loading, operation, and quality inspection widespread in manufacturing. Human workers monitor equipment, handle setups, and address exceptions.

title: Microbiologists
rationale: Lab-based research with automated systems handling many routine procedures. Novel experimental work still requires human researchers. The core work is scientific analysis and interpretation.

title: Middle school teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal. No significant physical automation potential.

title: Military careers
rationale: Extremely diverse roles from combat to logistics to administration. Some military logistics and support functions see robotic systems. Autonomous vehicles and drones expand. But combat, peacekeeping, and many field operations require human judgment in unpredictable environments. Average across all military roles.

title: Mining and geological engineers
rationale: Engineering design and planning work. Primarily knowledge-based with some site visits. The role is about mine design and optimization rather than physical extraction.

title: Models
rationale: Physical appearance-based work. While AI-generated models exist for some digital applications, live modeling for fashion shows, commercial shoots, and fitting sessions requires human presence. The industry values authentic human presentation.

title: Music directors and composers
rationale: Creative and leadership work in music. Composition is knowledge-based, and conducting requires human artistic interpretation and leadership.

title: Musicians and singers
rationale: Performance art requiring human creativity and expression. Live music is valued for its human element. No physical automation potential for live performance.

title: Natural sciences managers
rationale: Management of scientific research teams. Entirely administrative and knowledge-based.

title: Network and computer systems administrators
rationale: Primarily digital system administration. Some physical server and network hardware management, but increasingly cloud-based and remote. The physical component is minor and decreasing.

title: News analysts, reporters, and journalists
rationale: Journalism and reporting work that is primarily about investigation, writing, and communication. No significant physical component.

title: Nuclear engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work for nuclear systems. Primarily knowledge-based and computational.

title: Nuclear medicine technologists
rationale: Patient-facing work administering radioactive materials and operating imaging equipment. Each patient requires individualized care and positioning. Safety-critical handling of radioactive materials requires human oversight. Trust and patient communication essential.

title: Nuclear technicians
rationale: Operation and monitoring of nuclear facilities. Some routine monitoring automated, but physical maintenance and inspection of nuclear systems requires human technicians with specialized training. Safety regulations mandate human oversight.

title: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
rationale: Advanced clinical practice requiring patient assessment, treatment decisions, and hands-on care. Each patient is unique. Trust and clinical judgment are paramount. Nurse midwives assist births in highly variable situations. Very resistant to physical automation.

title: Nursing assistants and orderlies
rationale: Routine physical patient care (bathing, feeding, mobility assistance) sees some robotic assistance. Robotic lift systems and mobility aids operational. However, the intimate nature of personal care, working in diverse settings, and need for human empathy and trust means human aides remain essential for many tasks.

title: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
rationale: Inspection and assessment work primarily involving observation, analysis, and compliance checking. Some automated monitoring assists, but the role is primarily analytical with physical site visits.

title: Occupational therapists
rationale: Therapeutic work requiring hands-on patient assessment and treatment in variable settings—homes, hospitals, schools. Each patient has unique functional limitations. Trust, creativity in adapting activities, and interpersonal skills are core. Very resistant to automation.

title: Occupational therapy assistants and aides
rationale: Hands-on patient support under OT supervision. Physical assistance with exercises and daily activities in variable settings. Each patient's needs differ. Some therapeutic equipment automated, but personal assistance and motivation require human presence.

title: Oil and gas workers
rationale: Extraction operations increasingly automated with automated drilling, monitoring, and some maintenance robots. Large-scale operations use significant automation. However, variable field conditions, equipment troubleshooting, and wellsite work in diverse environments still require human workers.

title: Operations research analysts
rationale: Purely analytical work involving mathematical optimization and modeling. No physical component.

title: Opticians
rationale: Patient-facing work fitting eyeglasses and contact lenses. Automated lens cutting and frame adjustment tools improve, but each patient's face and prescription is unique. The fitting, adjustment, and customer service aspects require human dexterity and interpersonal skills.

title: Optometrists
rationale: Clinical eye examinations requiring patient interaction, skilled use of diagnostic equipment, and clinical judgment. Each patient presents unique conditions. Trust and communication essential. While automated screening tools assist, comprehensive eye care requires human practitioners.

title: Orthotists and prosthetists
rationale: Custom fabrication and fitting of orthotic and prosthetic devices for individual patients. Each device is customized to unique anatomy. 3D scanning and printing assist fabrication, but fitting, adjustment, and patient interaction require human skill and empathy.

title: Painters, construction and maintenance
rationale: Large commercial surfaces (warehouses, apartment buildings) increasingly painted by robotic systems. Spray-painting of uniform surfaces highly automatable. However, residential interior painting, detail work, prep work on variable surfaces, and custom finishes still require human painters.

title: Painting and coating workers
rationale: Industrial painting and coating—automotive, furniture, appliances—heavily automated with robotic spray systems. Standardized production lines use automated coating extensively. Powder coating and e-coating fully automated. Human workers handle custom work and quality oversight.

title: Paralegals and legal assistants
rationale: Legal research and document preparation work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Personal financial advisors
rationale: Advisory and client management work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.

title: Pest control workers
rationale: Work in diverse residential and commercial environments. Each infestation and building is different. Some automated monitoring and treatment systems exist, but inspecting variable structures, identifying pest entry points, and applying treatments in diverse settings requires human judgment and adaptability.

title: Petroleum engineers
rationale: Engineering design and analysis work. Primarily knowledge-based and computational.

title: Pharmacists
rationale: Automated dispensing systems handle majority of routine prescription filling. Robotic pharmacy systems operational in many hospitals and large retail pharmacies. Pharmacists shift to clinical consulting, patient counseling, and medication therapy management. The physical dispensing is largely automated.

title: Pharmacy technicians
rationale: Routine prescription filling, counting, and packaging heavily automated. Robotic pharmacy systems handle standardized dispensing. Human technicians focus on special preparations, insurance issues, and tasks automated systems cannot handle. High-volume pharmacies substantially automated.

title: Phlebotomists
rationale: Blood drawing requires patient interaction, vein identification in variable anatomy, and skilled needle insertion. Each patient's veins and anxiety levels differ. Trust and patient comfort essential. Automated blood-draw devices exist for some settings but patient variability limits adoption.

title: Photographers
rationale: Creative visual work requiring artistic vision and adaptation to variable subjects and conditions. While automated camera technology improves, professional photography is about creative interpretation, client interaction, and artistic judgment.

title: Physical therapist assistants and aides
rationale: Hands-on patient care guiding exercises and providing physical support. Each patient's condition and progress differs. Trust and motivation essential. Some robotic exercise equipment assists, but personal guidance and manual therapy techniques require human touch and judgment.

title: Physical therapists
rationale: Clinical assessment and hands-on treatment requiring skilled touch, patient communication, and real-time adaptation to patient responses. Each patient presents unique conditions. Trust and therapeutic relationship essential. Very resistant to physical automation.

title: Physician assistants
rationale: Clinical practice involving patient examination, diagnosis, and treatment. Each patient is unique. Requires trust, communication, and hands-on clinical skills. While diagnostic tools improve, the physical examination and patient interaction remain human.

title: Physicians and surgeons
rationale: Complex clinical practice and surgery. Robotic surgical systems assist with standardized procedures, but surgeons still direct and oversee. Diagnosis requires nuanced physical examination and patient interaction. Each patient is unique. Trust is paramount.

title: Physicists and astronomers
rationale: Research work with some experimental/observational components. The core work is theoretical and analytical. Lab/observatory work involves some physical equipment but is secondary.

title: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters
rationale: Work in highly variable residential and commercial environments. Each building has unique plumbing configurations and challenges. Troubleshooting leaks, working in tight spaces, and adapting to existing infrastructure requires human dexterity and judgment.

title: Podiatrists
rationale: Clinical foot and ankle care requiring patient examination, diagnosis, and treatment. Each patient presents unique conditions. Surgical procedures require skilled dexterity. Trust and communication essential.

title: Police and detectives
rationale: Law enforcement in unpredictable environments requiring split-second human judgment, de-escalation, investigation, and community interaction. Each situation is unique. Public trust and authority dynamics are inherently human. Surveillance technology assists but officers remain essential.

title: Political scientists
rationale: Research and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Postal service workers
rationale: Mail sorting heavily automated with robotic systems. Delivery routes increasingly use autonomous vehicles for some segments. Counter service declining. However, residential last-mile delivery in diverse neighborhoods and buildings still requires human carriers for many routes.

title: Postsecondary education administrators
rationale: Administrative and management work in higher education. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Postsecondary teachers
rationale: Teaching and research at colleges and universities. Fundamentally interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical automation potential.

title: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers
rationale: Power plant operations increasingly automated with remote monitoring and automated control systems. Routine operations handled by automated systems. Human operators focus on anomaly response, maintenance coordination, and complex decisions. Some plants approach lights-out operation.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
rationale: Management and educational leadership work. Entirely administrative and interpersonal.

title: Preschool teachers
rationale: Teaching very young children requires extreme human sensitivity, improvisation, and emotional care. Each child needs individual attention. Among the most interpersonal occupations. No automation potential.

title: Private detectives and investigators
rationale: Investigation work in highly variable environments. Each case is unique. While surveillance technology assists, physical investigation, interviews, and undercover work require human adaptability and judgment.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
rationale: Supervision and counseling work that is entirely interpersonal. Requires trust, human judgment, and communication. No physical component.

title: Producers and directors
rationale: Creative management and artistic direction. Entirely knowledge-based leadership work.

title: Project management specialists
rationale: Planning, coordination, and management work. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
rationale: Property inspection and valuation work. Each property is unique. While automated valuation models assist, physical inspection of diverse properties in variable conditions still requires human judgment. The inspection component is secondary to analytical work.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
rationale: Management work overseeing properties. Some maintenance coordination involves physical oversight, but the role is primarily administrative and interpersonal.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
rationale: Patient care in psychiatric facilities requiring trust, de-escalation, and interpersonal skills. Each patient's needs and episodes are unpredictable. Physical assistance needed in variable situations. Human presence and judgment essential for safety and therapeutic relationships.

title: Psychologists
rationale: Assessment and therapy work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
rationale: Communication strategy and management work. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Public relations specialists
rationale: Media relations and communication work. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
rationale: Communication and coordination work from dispatch centers. While technology-intensive, the role involves no physical labor—it's real-time decision-making and communication.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
rationale: Procurement and negotiation work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Quality control inspectors
rationale: Automated visual inspection and sensor-based quality control widespread in manufacturing. Machine vision systems handle most routine inspection tasks. Human inspectors focus on complex assessments, final acceptance, and non-standard products. High-volume production inspection substantially automated.

title: Radiation therapists
rationale: Patient-facing work positioning patients and operating radiation equipment. Each patient requires careful positioning and monitoring. Trust and communication essential. Robotic positioning assists but human oversight and patient interaction remain critical for safety.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
rationale: Patient-facing imaging work requiring positioning patients and operating equipment. Each patient's anatomy and condition varies. Trust and communication needed. AI assists image interpretation but physical patient handling and positioning requires human operators.

title: Railroad workers
rationale: Rail operations increasingly automated with autonomous train systems operational on many freight routes. However, maintenance, switching, and yard operations in variable conditions still require human workers. Crew requirements declining but not eliminated.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
rationale: Sales and advisory work that is entirely interpersonal. Virtual tours exist but the core work is client relationships and negotiation.

title: Receptionists
rationale: Front desk roles increasingly replaced by digital kiosks and automated check-in systems. However, many organizations still value human receptionists for visitor management, complex inquiries, and hospitality. The physical component (greeting, directing) is moderate.

title: Recreation workers
rationale: Leading recreational activities and programs for diverse groups. Requires human engagement, creativity, and adaptation to participants' needs. Each session and group is different. The interpersonal and improvisational aspects resist automation.

title: Recreational therapists
rationale: Therapeutic work using recreational activities for patient rehabilitation. Each patient has unique needs. Requires trust, creativity, and adaptation. The interpersonal and therapeutic aspects are core.

title: Registered nurses
rationale: Direct patient care requiring trust, communication, clinical assessment, and hands-on nursing skills. Each patient is unique. Robotic assistance for some tasks (medication dispensing, vital sign monitoring), but bedside nursing care, patient advocacy, and clinical judgment remain human. Emotional support is core.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
rationale: Counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Respiratory therapists
rationale: Patient care involving operation of respiratory equipment and patient assessment. Each patient's respiratory needs differ. Trust and communication essential. Some monitoring automated, but therapeutic interventions and patient interaction require human operators.

title: Retail sales workers
rationale: Self-service and automated checkout expanding. Some inventory management automated. However, customer assistance, product knowledge, and sales interaction remain human in many retail settings. High-end and specialty retail values human service. Lower-end retail sees more automation.

title: Roofers
rationale: Work at heights on variable rooftops. Each roof has unique pitch, material, and condition. Weather-exposed outdoor work. Some commercial flat-roof applications see limited automation, but the variety of residential roofing and the physical environment strongly resist robotic automation.

title: Sales engineers
rationale: Technical sales combining engineering knowledge with client relationships. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.

title: Sales managers
rationale: Sales leadership and strategy work. Entirely management and interpersonal.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
rationale: Counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
rationale: Office administrative work that is entirely desk-based. No physical component beyond basic office activities.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
rationale: Financial sales and advisory work. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal based.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
rationale: Patrol robots and automated surveillance systems handle routine monitoring of commercial facilities. However, human guards still needed for response, de-escalation, access control with judgment, and work in variable environments. Large facilities use robotic patrol as supplement.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
rationale: Semiconductor fabrication highly automated in cleanroom environments. Robotic wafer handling, automated processing equipment, and precise environmental controls dominate. Human technicians monitor, maintain, and troubleshoot but the actual processing is overwhelmingly automated.

title: Set and exhibit designers
rationale: Creative design work for unique sets and exhibits. Each project is custom. Physical construction may be involved but the role is primarily about creative design and direction. The uniqueness of each project resists automation.

title: Sheet metal workers
rationale: Factory-based sheet metal fabrication (cutting, bending, forming) highly automated with CNC equipment and robotic handling. However, on-site installation in HVAC systems, ductwork in variable buildings, and custom work requires human skill. Split between automated fabrication and manual installation.

title: Skincare specialists
rationale: Personal service requiring client trust, touch sensitivity, and adaptation to individual skin conditions. Each client's skin is unique. The spa/wellness experience is interpersonal. While some automated facial devices exist, the personal care and assessment aspects resist automation.

title: Small engine mechanics
rationale: Repair of diverse small engines (lawn mowers, chainsaws, boats) with each problem unique. Variable working conditions. While diagnostic tools improve, the physical repair work on many different equipment types in small shop environments requires human dexterity and problem-solving.

title: Social and community service managers
rationale: Management and program development work. Entirely administrative and interpersonal.

title: Social and human service assistants
rationale: Client-facing social service work that is entirely interpersonal. Helping people navigate social services requires human empathy and judgment.

title: Social workers
rationale: Client-facing counseling and advocacy work. Entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Sociologists
rationale: Research and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
rationale: Entirely digital work writing code and designing software systems. No physical component.

title: Solar photovoltaic installers
rationale: Rooftop installation in variable environments. Each roof and installation is different. Some large-scale ground-mount solar farms see automated installation of panels in uniform arrays. But residential rooftop work at heights with variable roof conditions requires human installers.

title: Special education teachers
rationale: Teaching students with disabilities requires extreme human sensitivity, patience, and individualized attention. Each student has unique needs. Fundamentally interpersonal with no automation potential.

title: Special effects artists and animators
rationale: Entirely digital creative work using software tools. No physical component.

title: Speech-language pathologists
rationale: Therapeutic work requiring patient assessment, trust, and personalized treatment. Each patient has unique speech and language challenges. The interpersonal and clinical assessment aspects are core. Some digital therapy tools assist but human therapists essential.

title: Stationary engineers and boiler operators
rationale: Operation and maintenance of building systems (boilers, HVAC, power). Routine monitoring increasingly automated. However, physical maintenance, troubleshooting, and emergency response in diverse building systems still requires human operators. Some facilities approach lights-out for routine operations.

title: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
rationale: Counseling work that is entirely interpersonal. Requires human empathy, trust, and therapeutic relationship.

title: Surgical assistants and technologists
rationale: Operating room assistance involving instrument handling and sterile technique. Robotic surgical systems handle some instrument positioning. However, the variety of surgical procedures, emergency situations, and need for real-time adaptation means human technologists remain essential for most surgeries.

title: Survey researchers
rationale: Research design and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based.

title: Surveying and mapping technicians
rationale: Fieldwork increasingly supplemented by drones, GPS, and automated survey equipment. Routine topographic surveys in open areas can be partially automated. However, complex site surveys in variable terrain, urban environments, and detailed boundary work still require human technicians.

title: Surveyors
rationale: Professional surveying in variable field conditions. While technology (GPS, drones, LiDAR) automates data collection, interpretation of boundary disputes, complex property surveys, and work in variable terrain requires human judgment and professional licensure.

title: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents
rationale: Desk-based analytical work reviewing tax returns and records. Entirely knowledge-based with some field visits.

title: Taxi drivers, shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs
rationale: Autonomous ride-hailing vehicles operational in many urban areas by 2031. Major cities have significant autonomous taxi fleets. However, complex urban environments, adverse weather, and luxury/personal chauffeur services still employ human drivers. The transition is well underway.

title: Teacher assistants
rationale: Supporting teachers in classroom settings. Interpersonal work with students requiring patience and adaptation. The role is about human interaction and student support.

title: Technical writers
rationale: Writing and documentation work that is entirely knowledge-based and digital.

title: Telecommunications technicians
rationale: Installation and repair of telecom equipment in variable buildings and facilities. Each site presents unique wiring and equipment configurations. While some standardized installations see limited automation, troubleshooting and repair in diverse environments requires human skill.

title: Tellers
rationale: ATMs and digital banking handle the vast majority of routine transactions. Many bank branches reduced or eliminated teller positions. Remaining tellers focus on complex transactions and customer service. The trend toward automation is well-established.

title: Top executives
