rationale: Leadership and strategic decision-making. Entirely about human judgment, vision, and organizational management.

title: Tour and travel guides
rationale: Interpersonal work providing guided experiences. Each tour involves unique group dynamics and real-time adaptation. While audio guides and virtual tours exist, live human guides are valued for personality, knowledge, and interaction.

title: Training and development managers
rationale: Management of training programs. Entirely administrative and strategic.

title: Training and development specialists
rationale: Designing and delivering training programs. Interpersonal and knowledge-based work.

title: Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
rationale: Management of logistics operations. Overseeing increasingly automated warehouses and transport, but the role is about planning, optimization, and human coordination.

title: Travel agents
rationale: Advisory and booking service work. Entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.

title: Tutors
rationale: One-on-one educational work requiring personalization and human connection. Each student has unique learning needs and styles.

title: Umpires, referees, and other sports officials
rationale: Officiating requires real-time human judgment in dynamic physical environments. While technology assists (instant replay, electronic line calling), human referees remain essential for game management, player interaction, and judgment calls in complex situations. Sports value the human element.

title: Urban and regional planners
rationale: Planning and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Veterinarians
rationale: Clinical care of diverse animal species in variable settings. Each animal and condition is unique. Surgery and examination require skilled dexterity with patients who can't communicate. Trust of pet owners essential. The variety of species and unpredictable animal behavior resists automation.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
rationale: Animal care involving feeding, cleaning, restraining, and assisting with procedures. Animals are unpredictable. Each animal's needs differ. Some routine feeding and cleaning in lab settings automated, but handling live animals requires human adaptability and care.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
rationale: Clinical support for veterinarians including restraining animals, administering treatments, and lab work. Each animal is unpredictable. Requires trust and skilled handling. Some lab procedures automated but direct animal care resists automation.

title: Waiters and waitresses
rationale: Robotic serving systems in some chain restaurants. However, full-service dining emphasizes human interaction, knowledge of menu, and hospitality. Carrying plates through variable dining rooms and providing personalized service requires human servers in most restaurants. Fast-casual sees more automation.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
rationale: Treatment plant operations increasingly automated with SCADA systems and remote monitoring. Routine operations handled automatically. Human operators focus on monitoring, troubleshooting, regulatory compliance, and responding to anomalies. Some plants approach near-autonomous operation.

title: Water transportation workers
rationale: Some cargo vessel operations see increased automation (autonomous container ships on fixed routes). However, variable waterway conditions, port operations, and passenger vessel work require human judgment. Inland waterway work in diverse conditions particularly resistant to automation.

title: Web developers and digital designers
rationale: Entirely digital work designing and coding websites. No physical component.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
rationale: Robotic welding dominant in manufacturing and production environments—automotive, structural steel, pipe fabrication. Automated welding systems handle most standardized joints. Human welders focus on field welding in variable positions, repair work, and custom fabrication. Production welding largely automated.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: Sales work involving client relationships and product knowledge. Entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: Maintenance and repair at extreme heights in variable weather conditions. Each turbine and failure mode is different. Working in confined nacelles requires human dexterity. Drone inspection assists but physical repair at height in wind remains challenging for robots.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: CNC routers and automated equipment handle most production woodworking—furniture manufacturing, cabinet production, millwork. Robotic finishing and assembly expanding. Custom and artisanal woodworking still requires human skill, but production volume is heavily automated.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: Creative writing work that is entirely knowledge-based. While AI writing tools assist, the creative and intellectual aspects are core. No physical component.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: Research work with some fieldwork in natural environments. The role is primarily about scientific observation and analysis. Fieldwork involves variable environments but is secondary to analytical work.
